title: DVB-T2 BICM AWGN campaign runner (binary + plot + reference data)
description:
## Goal

A reusable CLI binary that runs the full DVB-T2 BICM AWGN simulation
for one (rate, modulation) configuration, producing a CSV curve, a
JSON tracing log, and an optional calibration smoke sweep. Six
invocations (3 rates × 2 modulations) reproduce every curve required
by the epic. PNG overlays vs the ETSI TR 102 831 reference are
produced by a separate plotting script, not by the binary itself.

## Context

This task is the consumer of:

- NEW-INFRA: resumable, observable `SimulationRunner`,
- NEW-1: DVB-T2 BCH+LDPC concatenated codec,
- 87a2402f: column-row bit interleaver,
- existing Gray-QAM mapper / demapper in
  `crates/gf2-coding/src/modem/`,
- a generalisation of the existing `BpskAwgnChannel` to a
  `QamAwgnChannel` for 16-QAM and 64-QAM.

The TP07a vector validation (4cdaf1c5) is a hard prereq so we know
the BICM chain matches the standard bit-exactly before throwing CPU
hours at FER curves.

Plotting is intentionally emitted-data-only: the binary writes CSV
and a separate script consumes that CSV plus the reference TOML to
produce the PNG overlay. This avoids pulling a Rust plotting backend
into the workspace dep tree.

Spec doc:
[`dev/active/152388f4-campaign-runner.md`](dev/active/152388f4-campaign-runner.md).

## Deliverables

1. New binary: `crates/gf2-coding/src/bin/dvb_t2_awgn_campaign.rs`
   (or a similarly named binary; placement in `src/bin/` matches the
   existing `sim_runner.rs`).
2. CLI accepts at minimum:
   - `--rate {1/2|2/3|3/4}`
   - `--modulation {16qam|64qam}`
   - `--esn0-range <start>:<stop>:<step>` (dB)
   - `--target-errors <N>` (default 100)
   - `--max-frames <N>`
   - `--seed <u64>`
   - `--output-dir <path>`
   - `--resume`
   - `--gpu` — opt-in HIP/ROCm dispatch (requires building with
     `--features hip`; falls back to CPU with a `tracing::warn!`
     event on GPU runtime failure). Until the HIP LDPC BP prototype
     (`719fb8de`) lands, `--gpu` may return a clear "GPU path not
     yet integrated" error; the CLI surface is reserved now so the
     runner does not need a breaking change later.
   - `--calibrate` — run a smoke sweep at small frame budget over a
     predicted Es/N0 bracket; mutually exclusive with
     `--esn0-range`. Output goes to
     `<output-dir>/calibration/`.
   - `--calibrate-frames <N>` (default 1000) — used with
     `--calibrate`.
   - `--calibrate-bracket <a:b:c>` — three explicit Es/N0 points;
     defaults to a per-MODCOD bracket derived from the ETSI TR 102
     831 reference around its FER=10⁻⁴ point.
3. Output layout under `<output-dir>/`:
   - `curve_<rate>_<mod>.csv` — columns: es_n0_db, fer, ber, frames,
     errors, mean_iters, wall_seconds (one row per SNR point).
   - `tracing.jsonl` — structured `tracing` log via NEW-INFRA.
   - `README.md` — invocation, RNG seed, host info, total wall-clock.
   - `checkpoints/` — per-SNR JSON files (NEW-INFRA format).
   - `calibration/calibration_<rate>_<mod>.csv` (only when
     `--calibrate`).
4. Plotting script in `dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/` (Python /
   gnuplot / matplotlib; choice recorded in CLAUDE.md and the
   binary's rustdoc) that consumes `curve_<rate>_<mod>.csv` plus the
   reference TOML and produces `curve_<rate>_<mod>.png`. Not invoked
   by CI; operator-run.
5. ETSI TR 102 831 reference points checked in as a small,
   hand-extracted TOML file under
   `crates/gf2-coding/data/dvb_t2_tr102831_reference.toml`. Per-MODCOD
   schema:

   ```toml
   [normal_r1_2_16qam]
   source = "TR 102 831 Fig X.Y"
   points = [[es_n0_db, fer], ...]
   ```

   One section per in-scope MODCOD; section headers cite the
   figure / table the points were read from.
6. `--resume` propagates through to NEW-INFRA's checkpoint behaviour
   so the binary inherits crash recovery for free.

## Success criteria

- [hard] Binary builds without warnings under
  `cargo build --workspace --all-features --release`.
- [hard] A smoke campaign (3 SNR points, small frame budget) completes
  end-to-end and produces the CSV, JSONL, README, and checkpoints.
- [hard] `--calibrate` produces a calibration CSV at the predicted
  Es/N0 bracket for the selected (rate, modulation) using
  `--calibrate-frames` frames per point.
- [hard] Killing the binary with SIGINT mid-run and re-invoking with
  `--resume` results in a final CSV that is byte-identical to an
  uninterrupted reference run with the same seed (integration test).
- [hard] Plotting script produces a PNG overlay (simulated vs ETSI
  TR 102 831 reference) from the campaign CSV and the reference TOML
  via a single non-interactive invocation; documented in the
  binary's rustdoc.
- [hard] CLAUDE.md updated to list the new binary, the plotting
  script, and the reference data file.
- [hard] No new `unsafe`; satisfies `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.

## Non-goals

- No interactive UI.
- No Rust-side plotting backend (e.g. `plotters`, `charming`).
- No production GPU integration. `--gpu` is a CLI-surface
  reservation; the production path lights up only when the HIP LDPC
  BP prototype (`719fb8de`) lands.
- No code refactoring beyond what is needed to plug 16-QAM / 64-QAM
  into the existing mapper / demapper.
- No new channel model (AWGN only).
- This task does NOT execute the production campaigns — that is
  `e4849f07`.
